experiment: one heaptrack-instrumented Linux WPE no-capture create/destroy cycle

probe.actions: Create one WebView, wait for initial load, destroy it, then sample for 30 seconds; no screenshot, MHTML, or Inspector command.

environment.scope_limit: Instrumented diagnostic probe only; not an uninstrumented baseline, product integration, hardware rendering, production sandbox, or docs/04 acceptance.

heaptrack_summary.reported_outstanding_allocations_note: The probe was ended with SIGTERM after the final sample. Heaptrack's reported outstanding allocations include process-lifetime allocations at termination and are not evidence of a leak.

peak_allocation_sites.interpretation: A peak allocation path through the software rasterizer and WPE plugin initialization; this peak is not a measurement of bytes retained after WebView destruction.
Heaptrack did not resolve the callsite to a module or symbol; this allocation peak cannot be attributed.

limitations: Heaptrack instrumentation changes allocation timing and memory use; its absolute values cannot be compared with the earlier uninstrumented approximately 41 MiB parent residual.
The peak allocation sites summarize maxima during the whole run and do not prove which allocations remained at destroy+30 seconds.
The single Xvfb/software-GL sample does not cover hardware GBM, a production sandbox, the full Alula workbench, or the docs/04 three-run startup/idle/edit/close protocol.
WPEWebProcess exited after widget disposal while WPENetworkProcess remained; the roughly 40 MiB uninstrumented parent residual remains unexplained.
